subject: Commercial structure: modular private deployment packaging and conditional credits
thread_text:
From: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@medbridgehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medbridgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment packaging — questions on credits & support ladder

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to clarify a few items before we share with finance:

1) Can you confirm whether the platform fee is assessed per-site or per-deployment for a multisite VPC (we plan to deploy to 3 data centers)?
2) Are migration/onboarding credits available if we commit to a 36-month term? If so, how are they applied (invoice credit vs. reduced platform fee)?
3) We need the SKU matrix split between runtime node licenses and SRE retainer/support tiers so our SOW provider can map costs.

I attached a short note from our side explaining the expected rollout timeline. Looking to get commercial clarity by end of week so we can route to legal.

Thanks,
Sophie Grant
Head of Platform Strategy
MedBridge Health
Attachment: rollout_timeline.docx (docx)

---
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@medbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Private deployment packaging — questions on credits & support ladder

Sophie — great to hear from you. Short answers up-front, details below and I've attached a draft SKU matrix + SOW stub.

1) Platform fee model: per-customer platform fee covers the control plane and observability across all sites by default (single platform fee). For customers who insist on per-site accounting we can offer a prorated per-site option (adds complexity to billing and slightly increases the effective rate).

2) Migration credits: for a 36-month committed term we typically offer a one-time implementation credit equal to 3 months of platform fee (applied as invoice credit in month 1) OR a lowered platform fee spread across the first 12 months — your choice. We can also convert part of that credit into an engineering onboarding retainer if you prefer guaranteed hours instead of cash credit.

3) SKU matrix: we separate runtime (node seats by GPU class), platform fee, and an on-call / SRE retainer. Support tiers are: Silver (business hours), Gold (24x7 basic), Platinum (24x7 + guaranteed response SLAs + named SRE). Attached workbook maps typical customer usage to node counts and recommended support tier.

Action items I propose:
- I’ll send a clean SOW (attached) with both credit flows and per-site vs. single-platform options by EOD Tuesday.
- Marissa will drop recommended support-tier language and SLA bullets you can use in procurement language.
- Ben will confirm whether the per-site billing route requires any additional contractual carveouts.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood-Onprem-SKU-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), MedBridge_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@medbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Private deployment packaging — questions on credits & support ladder

Looping in a quick commercial note on the per-site ask — Sophie, if MedBridge wants per-site invoicing (three distinct invoices tied to separate legal entities/POs) we can support it but we need to lock the commit at the aggregate level and add a 5% administrative overlay to cover separate billing and reconciliation. That overlay is negotiable for strategic pilots.

On credits: the most straightforward path for your finance team is an invoice credit in month 1 (simple accounting). Spreading the reduction across 12 months creates amortization complexity for you. If finance prefers amortization we can model both in the SOW — I’ll include a sample journal entry illustration.

Also — recommend you consider a blended node SKU for your first 12 months: reserve a pool of spot-capable nodes and a smaller guaranteed low-latency pool. That lets you keep platform fee steady while optimizing runtime cost. I put a sample split in the attached SKU workbook.

Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---
From: Elliot Shaw <elliot.shaw@medbridgehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@medbridgehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Private deployment packaging — questions on credits & support ladder

Ava/Ben/Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. Procurement has reviewed and we are fine with the following commercial approach:

- Single aggregated platform fee for the customer (covers all three sites).
- 36-month term with a 3-month platform fee implementation credit applied as invoice credit in month 1.
- We accept the proposal to convert up to 50% of the credit into an engineering onboarding retainer (MedBridge will confirm split within two weeks).
- Support: Gold tier for production (24x7 basic). We may upgrade to Platinum during BAU-to-scale phase.
- Please deliver a redline-ready SOW and a sample invoice showing the credit application; procurement wants the invoice model to match our accounting, so invoice credit preferred.

Elliot Shaw
Procurement Manager, MedBridge Health
Attachment: MB_Procurement_approval.pdf (pdf)

>

>
> Ava
